title: A benzofuran–thiazole Schiff-base fluorescent probe for rapid and sensitive determination of tetracycline in environmental and food samples
content: Tetracycline (TC) contamination in environmental and food matrices is an increasing concern due to its extensive use and persistence, highlighting the need for sensitive and selective sensing strategies. Herein, a novel benzofuran–thiazole Schiff-base fluorescent probe, 2-(((4-(benzofuran-2-yl)thiazol-2-yl)imino)methyl)phenol (WS-2), was rationally designed and synthesized for rapid TC detection. The structure of WS-2 was confirmed by FTIR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, elemental analysis, and UV-vis spectroscopy, while density functional theory (DFT) calculations provided insight into its electronic structure and intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) characteristics. Under optimized conditions (pH 8.0 and λex = 290 nm), WS-2 exhibited intense fluorescence emission at 373 nm with a large Stokes shift of approximately 118 nm. Addition of TC induced a rapid fluorescence quenching response, reaching equilibrium within 3 min, over a wide concentration range of 0.01–40 µM. The sensing response is proposed to involve hydrogen-bond-assisted molecular recognition between TC and WS-2, perturbing the ICT process and promoting fluorescence quenching. The probe exhibited excellent analytical performance, with a detection limit of 3 × 10−3 µM, a linearity of R2 = 0.998, and high selectivity toward TC in the presence of common organic compounds and metal ions. The practical applicability of WS-2 was demonstrated by determining TC in environmental water and food samples, including apple, tomato, and honey. Satisfactory recoveries of 97–103% were obtained, with relative standard deviations below 2.0%. These results demonstrate the potential of WS-2 as a simple, rapid, sensitive, selective, and reliable fluorescent sensing platform for routine TC monitoring in diverse environmental and food matrices.
